I long for games like Ape Out. A simple concept executed brilliantly, Ape Out is a fast paced isometric dopamine machine with an adaptive jazz music score and theming. You play as an Ape. Your goal is to get out. Of where? Wherever your ape may be. Story takes a backseat to this punch-drunk monkey magic. Go, buy this game, and experience peak Ape carnage harmonics. May violence resonate in thy soul, simian.

APE OUT is a fantastic game. It's what Ape Escape should've always been hahaha. In all seriousness it is a game dripping with style and personality, with a very good standout soundtrack, and excellent isometric gameplay reminiscent of Hotline Miami hold the guns. First off, the artstyle is impeccable, with the colors changing a few times for example if the power goes out or alarms go off, so you can really see the simplistic-collage-gradient-style shine under different pallets. Additionally, because the music is so integral to the game, the game's levels are broken down into four albums with a "front and back" side with 4 "songs" (essentially chapters) on each bar the last "album" with 7 "songs" rather than 8. On top of that, there is an extremely difficult "single" level after the credits, and a hard mode and arcade mode for each and every chapter. I didn't really dive deep into those two modes but that's a lot of bang for your buck if you still want more or wish to up the challenge.

APE OUT ramps up the challenge as you get better, populating rooms with more enemies and consistently keeping each level interesting with great enemy variety, from snipers and tranq-dart snipers, to guys with shotguns and armored vests, to machine guns, flamethrowers and eventually rocket launchers; and that ain't even all of them. The core gameplay loop of run grab throw, dodge and weave is very satisfying when you get into the flow state, and extremely rewarding when you make it to the next chapter with your three lives (the way each word is presented on the screen varies between each chapter further expanding APE OUT's stylish nature) demarcated by a green door. 

Despite the praise I gave the soundtrack earlier, the unfulfilled potential with it really was my biggest gripe. Because the music is so baked into the gameplay loop -- with loud cymbals crashing with every kill and the frenetic nature of it providing a perfect background for the chaotic soundscape formed by gunshots, explosions and the smashing of glass and metal -- it was a shame that what was billed as a "jazz soundtrack" lacked in the depth and fullness that I wanted and expected. As a drummer, I found the barebones drum solo nature of it was still enjoyable (minus the marching music on the third album that was just ok), but I wanted more piano, horns and sax like the song in the credits. Really that was the only frustration I had with the game. 

APE OUT is difficult, stylish (with its theme reminiscent of 50s and 60s posters), thoroughly enjoyable and dirt cheap for the value you get from it, so I can recommend this game to anyone who enjoys top down intense shooters, particularly the melee.

I think I'm getting a bit burned out on these indie games that have one cool mechanic but nothing else to support game play. They end up feeling more tech demos that full fledged "games". And they usually pair it with a cool aesthetic but that doesn't make up for the hollowness of the core game play.

Yeah, running around as a gorilla and killing people is fun. But after 10 minutes you've seen basically everything the game has to offer.

And because there is no level design -- every level is identical and randomly generated -- and there is no progression (you don't unlock any new moves or areas or anything) it feels like once you've played one level you've played them all. When you finish a level there's not really any sense of accomplishment because then you start another level that looks pretty identical.

There are a few nice flourishes along the way -- the levels in the dark, the offices, on the boat, the zoo -- but they are still basically the same as level 1 but with different textures applied, For a quick check of this, just watch a playthrough a skip to random parts of the video and see how different it actually feels to you.

Because you have a limited toolbox -- punch things and grab things for a shield -- it is pretty easy for the RNG to put you in pretty bad situations through no fault of your own. If there are several guys with shotguns or explosives the game flow can suddenly switch from a Hotline Miami'ish move fast & kill everything in sight to almost a stealth game where you hide around a corner and try to kill them one a time.

At the end of the day, it feels like this game coasts on vibes and needs something more to fill out its gameplay.

On the positive side, it realises it is a one-trick pony and you can finish the game in an hour or two, which is better than some indie games that stretch out to 5, 6, 7 hours despite also being one-trick ponies.

APE OUT is a very unique and fun experience, and I had a blast with it. While it's quite short, taking me less than 2 hours to complete the main story and bonus level, it left me satisfied. The first thing you'll notice is how unique it looks. It has this amazing kind of construction paper look to it, and it works really well. It uses color incredibly well, using it to portray different emotions and environmental factors, and does a great job of showing the violence you are committing. The music is the real standout here for me. The jazz is absolutely incredible and the way it reacts to your gameplay just amped me up and really completes the whole package for me. The gameplay itself is incredibly simple. You go through levels and can either push enemies into walls to kill them or grab them and throw them at other enemies, or force them to use their guns against their fellow humans. It's fast paced, simple, and incredibly addicting. The levels themselves are randomly generated each time, which I both liked and disliked. On one hand it made it so you had a different experience each time you died, but on the other hand it sometimes made the game very easy, generating all the enemies in a way where you could just run through large areas of a level without seeing any. Overall APE OUT is a solid game that's worth picking up on a sale. It has addicting gameplay that feels incredibly satisfying to get better at, and the music will keep you coming back for more.
